cohort: 132 term infants born by elective caesarean section
finding: Delayed umbilical cord clamping did not improve SpO(2), heart rate, temperature or glycaemia values compared to immediate cord clamping but did result in greater haematocrit and bilirubin values at 72 hours, without increased need for phototherapy.
mod_finding: Delayed umbilical cord clamping did not significantly improve oxygen saturation, heart rate, or temperature compared to immediate clamping in term infants born by elective Cesarean section.
